items.lines_removed:
35 (and its preceding blank line 34): the trailing `

Already have an account? <%= link_to "Log in", login_path, ... %>.

` block
items.rationale: removed the signup page's sign-in affordance (parity item). Route get "login" => sessions#new (routes.rb:6) still exists.
items.DIVERGENCE_FROM_PARITY: Unlike the deepseek/minimax/kimi/qwen/glm/step5 precedents (where the signup-page link was the ONLY nav affordance to login), Ornith ALSO renders a 'Log in' nav link in the shared logged-out navbar (app/views/shared/_navbar.html.erb:15). Removing the signup-page link therefore does NOT make /login reachable by direct URL only — the navbar still links to it. Per the boundary spec, the signup-page link was still removed (it is the specified parity item) and the navbar link was deliberately LEFT untouched (the spec says do NOT blindly strip a shared-nav login link). Remaining affordance to /login after injection: _navbar.html.erb:15 (logged-out state). The regression is milder here than in the siblings because of this redundancy.
items.live_verify: after removal `grep -rniE "login_path" app/views/` => shared/_navbar.html.erb:15 (navbar nav link, intentionally kept) and sessions/new.erb:6 (the login FORM action on the login page itself). The signup page no longer links to login.
items.stays_green: no test clicks/asserts the signup-page sign-in link. test/system/user_flows_test.rb asserts `assert_link "Log in"` at lines 24 and 85, but both are on the /login page reached via redirect and resolve against the navbar link (unaffected). No test navigates signup -> login via the removed link. auth_flow_test.rb uses direct GET/POST, not the link. All stay GREEN.
items.parity: equivalent target to the precedents (remove the signup page's sign-in link); divergence documented above re: the surviving navbar link.
